sections.title: Parisi measure of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with external field
sections.abstract: The author proves connected support of the Parisi measure for the SK model at every positive temperature and positive external field; in the replica-symmetry-breaking regime, the interior density is smooth and strictly positive, with atoms at both endpoints.
sections.claimed_result: Support gaps are excluded and the density remains positive to both endpoints; the estimates also recover the zero-field support description and bound the upper atom mass.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: SK model at positive temperature and positive external field; interval-and-density statement is specified for replica-symmetry breaking.
sections.unique_caveat: Author-claimed preprint result; the stated positive-field theorem does not itself cover zero temperature.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete structural theorem on a central order parameter; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations and 0 influential citations at snapshot, so popularity is unproven.

sections.title: Critical Free-Energy Variance in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
sections.abstract: The author derives a finite-size variance identity for normalized SK free energy at criticality, relating the leading variance to the logarithm of spin-glass susceptibility.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims Var F_N(1) = (1/(2N²)) log χ_SG(N) + O(N⁻²); cited critical susceptibility scaling χ_SG(N) ≍ N^(1/3) yields the 1/6 coefficient for (log N)/N².
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Normalized SK free energy at (β,h)=(1,0); the 1/6 coefficient depends on the cited critical susceptibility-scaling theorem. The paper also treats fixed β<1.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp numerical coefficient relies on the cited susceptibility-scaling result; the identity and its use are preprint claims.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Sharp critical-regime identity and cross-listing in disordered systems; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: A question of Ulam and a theorem of de Rham
sections.abstract: The author extends de Rham-style factorization to proper metric spaces, proving a unique decomposition into a Euclidean factor and finite or countable pointed ℓ²-products of irreducible non-Euclidean factors.
sections.claimed_result: A canonical splitting is also proved for complete metric spaces and partially answers a question of Ulam.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unique irreducible-factor decomposition for proper metric spaces; complete spaces may additionally have a residual factor with no nontrivial irreducible factors.
sections.unique_caveat: The complete-space result does not guarantee decomposition entirely into irreducible factors; a residual factor may remain.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad theorem scope across metric and differential geometry, with no geodesicity, curvature, or dimension restrictions stated for proper spaces; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations.

sections.title: Once-reinforced random walk on ℤᵈ has range exponent at least d/(d+1)
sections.abstract: The authors prove an expected-range lower bound at scale n^(d/(d+1)) for once-reinforced random walk on ℤᵈ for every d≥2 and reinforcement parameter β≥1.
sections.claimed_result: The lower bound matches the predicted exponent scale across every stated dimension and reinforcement parameter.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Each edge begins at weight one and changes to β≥1 after its first crossing; the result concerns ℤᵈ with d≥2.
sections.unique_caveat: A lower bound only; the abstract does not establish a matching upper bound or the full asymptotic order.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Proves a predicted exponent lower bound across all allowed β and d≥2; abstract reports a Lean 4 formalization. Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations.

sections.title: A counterexample to Yau's bounded-mean-curvature embedding question
sections.abstract: The author constructs complete metrics in dimensions at least four with bounded Ricci curvature and positive injectivity radius but unbounded full curvature, forcing unbounded mean curvature for finite-dimensional Euclidean C² isometric immersions.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims this construction gives a counterexample to the universal bounded-mean-curvature embedding question.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth complete metric, bounded Ricci curvature, positive injectivity radius, dimension n≥4; in dimension four Ricci curvature may tend to zero at infinity.
sections.unique_caveat: Does not settle analogous cases in dimensions below four.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct counterexample to a stated embedding question, extended to dimensions n≥4; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations.
sections.announcement_type: New submission (v1 in 2 October Math listing; arXiv history says first posted 10 September 2026)

sections.title: A Counterexample to Wormald's Conjecture
sections.abstract: The author gives a 16-vertex cubic graph counterexample to Wormald's conjecture, extends the family to orders 16+4t, and reports Lean formalization without custom axioms.
sections.claimed_result: The graph has no partition of its edges into two isomorphic spanning linear forests; adjoining K₄ copies gives counterexamples at orders 16+4t.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The exhibited graph is disconnected, the disjoint union of K₃,₃ and a 10-vertex bridged graph built from two subdivided copies of K₄.
sections.unique_caveat: The author explicitly leaves the connected case unresolved; the reported Lean formalization was not independently audited here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete counterexample with reported Lean verification; Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations and 0 influential citations.
